Questions: From the file 1- J2004-P-RPT-0010_1.pdf, what are the major equipment components included in the HC-2 heater system?
Expected Response: HC-2 heater (FH-102), exhaust stack (ST-100), burner (BRN-101), combustion air blowers (BL-101), and primary circulation pumps (P-100A/100B/100C).

Questions: From the file 1- J2004-P-RPT-0010_1.pdf, what safety interlocks are monitored during the standby cycle?
Expected Response: Burner flame scanner (BE 20001) and proof of closure switches (ZSC 20001, 20002, 20004, 20005) on fuel train safety shutoff valves.

Questions: From the file 1- J2004-P-RPT-0010_1.pdf, what is the process fluid and its operating conditions in the HC-2 heater?
Expected Response: Therminol 59, heated from 140°C to 170°C with a total system flow of 979,850 kg/hr, providing 17,704 kW of heat.

Questions: From the file 1- J2004-P-RPT-0010_1.pdf, what happens if a burner interlock fails during operation?
Expected Response: The system shuts down, locks out, and requires a manual reset at the BMS display; a common alarm (BA 20001) is sent to the Customer’s DCS/PLC.

Questions: From the file 1- J2004-P-RPT-0010_1.pdf, what are the steps in the pre-purge sequence of the HC-2 heater?
Expected Response: BMS sends a blower start command, opens the combustion air damper to high fire, verifies safety interlocks within 10 seconds, and conducts a preset purge time based on four air exchanges.

Questions: From the file 1- J2004-P-RPT-0010_1.pdf, how is the burner firing rate controlled in auto mode?
Expected Response: By a PID control loop using the process outlet temperature (TE/TIT/TI/TC 27002), adjusting the fuel gas and combustion air damper actuators (TZ 20000, TZ 25002).

Questions: From the file 1- J2004-P-RPT-0010_1.pdf, what instrumentation is used to monitor low process fluid flow?
Expected Response: Flow sensors (FE/FIT/FY 27002–27008) across orifice plates in each coil outlet, set to detect 90% (LL1) and 75% (LL2) of full flow.

Questions: From the file 1- J2004-P-RPT-0010_1.pdf, what is the role of the high flue gas temperature sensor (TE/TIT/TY 25001)?
Expected Response: Monitors flue gas temperature in the stack; if it exceeds the setpoint, the BMS shuts down the burner and locks out, requiring a manual reset.

Questions: From the file 1- J2004-P-RPT-0010_1.pdf, how are the primary pumps (P-100A/100B/100C) controlled?
Expected Response: Started/stopped by the Customer’s DCS based on permissives (XI 30001–30003) from the Sigma PLC, ensuring sufficient expansion tank level and pressure.
